ensure-username: the deployed Node module imported usernameForRequest from _username.js, where it does not exist (a latent TypeError). This port implements the documented contract: claim an explicit handle, otherwise repair/assign one.
Token verification rejects a non-RS256 alg, a missing kid, an unknown kid (after one forced JWKS refetch), a missing sub, a future iat and an expired exp, in addition to aud/iss.
A Firestore ABORTED is retried (including at commit time) up to 4 times with backoff; an exhausted conflict is surfaced as the same 500 the Node runtime produced.

Balances: wallet sign-in/link still seed and merge the Firestore balances document exactly as Node did (increment(0) seed, integer merge for a claimed wallet-only account). No new SQL ledger table was created in this crate; the commerce worker's pokoin_account_balances/pokoin_ledger_entries remain the single money writer.

GET+OPTIONS. The React Portfolio/Explore BFF: Pokoin catalog rows plus the native listing overlay, PKN only, Pokoin CDN art only. Never CardTrader image hosts (blanked), never the candyext dump. Game scoping ported in full from _marketplace_game + the 23-game INGEST_GAMES table: query game/marketplaceGame, then the x-pokoin-game/x-marketplace-game header, then x-pokoin-host/x-forwarded-host/x-original-host/host/origin subdomain detection, and each non-Pokemon game resolves its OWN catalog database (explicit per-game env, else derived from the base URL host) through a lazily-created pool. Limits follow the game (Pokemon 400/500, others 2000/2500). The catalog query adapts to which relations exist (to_regclass probe for marketplace_user_listings and cheapest_homepage_cache_blueprint) and to whether the request is a by-id lookup, the Pokemon priced path, or the plain catalog list; a missing relation is an empty catalog (200) while any other error is a 500. Row shaping is byte-faithful to _marketplace_react_card: cdn.pokoin.com rewritten to same-origin /card-images, previews kept out of the grid image, a foreign leftover key (another card's picture, e.g. an old halved ct_id/2 prefix) dropped with the card's own homepage webp used as the tile, integral JS numbers serialized without a decimal point, and set rollups sorted by value. CORS is GET/OPTIONS with Content-Type+Authorization and Max-Age 86400; success carries public, max-age=15, s-maxage=30 (plus stale-while-revalidate=60 except for the by-id empty case). Reads only existing tables; no new SQL. Not exercised against live Postgres.

The whole pricing core is ported and unit-tested: CardTrader sold medians only, sliced by blueprint+condition+language+reverse/1st-edition/graded with the CardTrader and Pokoin condition/language spellings collapsed onto one key; the 20x joke-listing outlier filter; last-sale carry-forward as a binary search; holdings counted from each slice's since day with unpriced slices excluded from the priced count; basket move restricted to slices priced on both days; the frozen-card-day protection that survives a 1-DR-only stock table but is discarded on a basis/revision change; and the 400-day day-by-day series with wallet carry-forward and a live today point. Handler behaviour verified: GET only with no-store on every response, 401 without a bearer, a fresh stored series served with zero SQL, a stale-but-current series served as the last good one when the market read model is missing, and an out-of-date basis discarded rather than served. Reads the existing marketplace_cardtrader_1dr_assets / marketplace_user_listings / marketplace_card_versions / cardtrader_sold_daily tables and writes portfolio_history/{uid}; no new tables. Not exercised against live Postgres/Firestore.

The full Associates desk: roster lookup by lower(btrim(email)), the campaign-window progress, and live earnings folded from the orders whose createdAt falls in the window. The IT->IT rule is ported exactly: buyer country from shippingAddressCountryCode or the single distinct shipments.toCountry, seller country from shipments.fromCountry or the listing row's seller_country (a second SQL pass), with unresolvable countries counted as unverified rather than guessed into the pool; refunds net the royalty base down and a fully refunded order contributes zero. Admins (claim or users/{uid} profile role/roles) additionally get the roster overview with one order load per distinct window. The 403 body keeps `associate: null`, and the CORS set is GET/OPTIONS with Authorization+Content-Type. This is also the first user of the new composite AND filter and the plain-JSON document view. Not exercised against live Postgres/Firestore.

Roster prefix search over public.marketplace_associates (display name or email), the LIKE-wildcard strip, the 5-row cap, and an auth+profile lookup per row that skips a roster entry without an account. Returns only public facts: display name, claimed username, role badge - never roster emails. Not exercised against live Postgres/Firebase.

Both verbs. POST builds the enriched prompt (market-first directive, personal intent, the raw user message, multi-card photo context, attached cards/photos, the reply-card directive), proxies to the Poko service with the shared token, resolves the cards Poko names against the marketplace_search_candidates catalog by exact id (card_id::text = any) then exact case-insensitive name (most-traded printing), strips the hidden [[cards: ...]] marker, and drops the desk/attached card from the echoed images. GET pages poko_conversations/{uid}/events 20 at a time using the Node limitToLast equivalence (newest DESC page reversed). User and assistant rows are written in ONE commit with the reply strictly after the question. When the assistant is unreachable the stored reply is the documented fallback with ok:false, source:'unavailable' and the paired error string, and the turn is still persisted; there is no locally scripted answer. Chat photos are only fetched from our own *.r2.dev/user-photos/ URLs, JPEG-checked and size-bounded, then sent to the scan service's multi-card mode and deduped. Per-IP comfort limit 20/min via the shared best-effort limiter. The photo identify and Hermes proxy are native HTTP through the crate transport; the transcript is Firestore poko_conversations/{uid}/events. No new SQL tables. Not exercised against live Firestore/Hermes/scan.

All six actions ported over the existing poko_telegram_link_codes / poko_telegram_links / poko_discord_links tables: create_code (8-char unambiguous alphabet, sha256 `poko-connect:{code}` never stores the raw code, 15-minute expiry, one live code per uid, expired rows pruned), redeem (single-use UPDATE guarded by `redeemed_at is null and expires_at > now()`, numeric-only Telegram/Discord ids, one Pokoin account per channel link), my_status, status, unlink and unlink_me with the Node back-compat quirks (no channel clears Telegram only; the default channel is reported as telegram). Service auth is a constant-time compare of POKO_MARKET_SERVICE_TOKEN/POKONTACT_SERVICE_TOKEN: no token -> 503, wrong token -> 401, unknown action -> 400 listing all six, and the Node `{error:'POST only'}` body for other verbs. Not exercised against live Postgres.

All nine actions: balances (25-id cap), set_consent, merge_wallet, stake, close, settle, refund, redeem_bonus, reward_game. PKN only moves user -> that round's escrow and escrow -> that round's stakers; the stake is checked against the balance INSIDE the transaction that debits it (available + previous >= amount, so raising a bet reuses the previous stake); closesAt is clamped to one 10-minute bet window and a closed/expired round is refused. The pari-mutuel split is a property-tested pure function: floors every winner share and gives the rounding remainder to the largest winning stake so sum(payouts) == sum(stakes) for every winner/loser/unit combination; no winners means a full refund; settle returns stored payouts with idempotent:true and writes nothing on a replay. A verified end-to-end test asserts the winner's balance is credited with the whole pot, the loser is untouched, the paired ledger entry is written, and the replay is a no-op. The Discord wallet merge is once per Discord account with the 200 PKN cap, the double-bonus forfeit and the frozen remainder. MONEY: writes the same balances/{key} + ledger_entries documents the platform uses, in ONE Firestore transaction, behind the public LedgerSink seam so the shared writer (commerce's store::apply) can be injected instead. No new SQL tables. Not exercised against live Firestore/Postgres.

action=get|sync with both auth modes: the Poko service token may act for any firebaseUid (persistOverlay=false), a Firebase bearer only for its own uid (persistOverlay=true). Reads the existing marketplace_user_recents, marketplace_user_listings, poko_user_personal_snapshot and marketplace_search_candidates tables (42P01/42703 tolerated per section, exactly like Node) plus the Firestore collection summary. sync persists the client overlay via an ON CONFLICT upsert with bigint[] + jsonb params. formatPersonalIntent is ported line for line, including the 'never invent ownership' preamble, the 8-row caps and the '~N PKN' cart total. Error shapes match Node: auth/action failures are a bare {error}, build failures are {ok:false, error:'Could not load personal context.'}. Not exercised against live Postgres/Firestore.

claimReferral with every Node guardrail: valid-code shape, unknown code (404 invalid_code), self-referral, the 14-day new-account window (409 not_new), no prior paid purchase/sale, circular invites, and the already-claimed short circuit. settleReferral pays both sides 20 PKN from the treasury with balanced ledger_entries in ONE Firestore transaction, enforces the 50-rewards-per-30-days referrer cap, returns treasury_low instead of overdrawing, and is idempotent through the pending status gate.

action=message, action=pay, action=read, action=photo and action=listing-photos. message/pay write the conversation, the event and (for pay) both balances plus both ledger_entries plus a notification in ONE Firestore transaction. pay is idempotent through payment_operations/{sha256(uid\0clientToken)}: a replay with the same peer and amount returns the original ledgerId, a different peer/amount is a 409, and an insufficient balance is a 400. Photos go to the user-photos R2 bucket through the crate's SigV4 client (private cache for chat, public for listing); listing-photos is an owner-scoped `photo_urls` UPDATE. Not exercised against live Firestore/R2/Postgres.

intake/bag/receive-hub/handoff and pending answer 501 `coming_soon`, which is exactly what the live Node handler returns because the Partner app is not launched - this is the real contract, not a stub of ours. Action resolution keeps Node's `cleanAction(query || body || 'directory')` order, so a whitespace action wins and cleans to empty instead of falling through. Unknown actions give 400 with the action list.
